description: A repository with Require tests on. The PR adds sha256Hex, which builds the x-amz-content-sha256 header CloudFront validates on signed uploads, in a package with no test runner. The reviewer checked it by hand and posted the missing test as 'a suggestion only', and the review approved. A required rule broken blocks whatever the model called it; no runner is not an exemption, so the finding asks for the runner and the test. A re-review of the same commit keeps the block, an answer explaining the missing runner doesn't settle it, and only the push that adds the runner and the test approves.

findings.title: sha256Hex check isn't kept as a test
findings.body: Verification step 2 compared sha256Hex with Node's createHash by hand. apps/cms has no test runner (no vitest in its package.json), so nothing keeps that check. When the package gets tests, a small case hashing a sample body that includes non-ASCII characters, compared with createHash('sha256').update(body, 'utf8').digest('hex'), would lock in the exact header CloudFront needs. This is a suggestion only.

comment.text: @coderhelm this package has no test runner, so I checked the hash by hand. Please re-review.

model.summary: Adds vitest and the hash test.
